name: CH32V203C8T6
title: CH32V203 series: 144 MHz 32-bit RISC-V microcontrollers with USB, CAN and a 12-bit ADC
summary: A family of general-purpose 32-bit microcontrollers on the QingKe V4B RISC-V core (RV32IMAC) running to 144 MHz with zero-wait flash. Models range from 20 to 64 pins with 32K to 128K of zero-wait flash and 10K to 64K of SRAM, and carry a full-speed USB device controller, a full-speed USB host/device controller, CAN 2.0B, up to four USARTs, two SPI, two I2C, two 12-bit ADCs with touch-key sensing, two op-amp/comparators, one advanced and three general-purpose timers. The supply is 2.4 V to 3.6 V (3.0 V to 3.6 V with USB), with a separate VBAT backup domain for the RTC. The CH32V203C8T6 is the 48-pin LQFP model with 64K flash and 20K SRAM.
key_figures: 32K / 64K / 128K by model; 224K total code flash (480K on V203RB)
LQFP48, 64K flash, 20K SRAM, 37 GPIO, 4 USART, 2 SPI, 2 I2C, CAN, USBD + USBHD
VDD 2.4 V to 3.6 V; 3.0 V to 3.6 V with USB; VBAT 1.8 V to 3.6 V
11.8 mA typ at 144 MHz, all peripherals on (V203)
TSSOP20, QFN20, QFN28, QSOP28, LQFP32, QFN32, LQFP48, QFN48X7, LQFP64M

notes: Every model has two watchdogs (WWDG and IWDG), a 64-bit SysTick, an RTC, a 144 MHz maximum CPU clock and a 3.3 V rated supply.
(1) The flash figure is the zero-wait region, R0WAIT. The rest of the code flash runs with wait states: 224K minus R0WAIT on most models, 480K minus R0WAIT on the V203RB.
(2) The 128K flash, 64K SRAM model can be set by option word to 128K + 64K, 144K + 48K or 160K + 32K of flash and SRAM.
(3) Timer functions that need pins (PWM, capture) exist only where the package brings those pins out.
The last character of the order code gives the temperature range: 6 for -40 to 85 °C, 7 for -40 to 105 °C.

circuits.title: Supply connections
circuits.description: The usual way to power the chip. A 1.8 V to 3.6 V cell feeds VBAT alone. The VDD rail goes to every VDDx and VIOx pin, with a 0.1 µF capacitor down to the VSSx ground, and the same VDD rail reaches VDDA with its own 0.1 µF capacitor to VSSA. All grounds are common.
notes: J_VBAT, J_VDDX, J_VSSX, J_VDDA and J_VSSA are the chip's pins of those names; on the LQFP48 VDDx/VIOx is pins 24, 36 and 48, VSSx pins 23, 35 and 47, VDDA pin 9, VSSA pin 8, VBAT pin 1.

circuits.title: 8 MHz crystal on OSC_IN and OSC_OUT
circuits.description: An 8 MHz crystal runs the high-speed oscillator: it sits across OSC_IN and OSC_OUT, and each end has a load capacitor to ground, CL1 and CL2, normally equal and sized for the crystal's specified load (20 pF is the recommendation for a crystal with 60 Ω series resistance).
notes: On the CH32V203RB the crystal is 32 MHz and the load capacitors are inside the chip, so C1 and C2 are left out.

circuits.title: 32.768 kHz crystal for the low-speed oscillator
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal across the low-speed oscillator pins, with a load capacitor from each end to ground. CL1 and CL2 are normally equal, about 12 pF each, chosen so that CL1 × CL2 / (CL1 + CL2) plus 2 pF to 7 pF of stray capacitance meets the crystal's load figure.
notes: Misprint: the two pins read OSC_IN and OSC_OUT; they should read OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT (PC14 and PC15).

circuits.title: Reset pin with push button
circuits.description: NRST has an internal pull-up of about 40 kΩ to VIO and a Schmitt input with a pulse filter. Outside, a 0.1 µF capacitor and a push button both connect NRST to ground.

circuits.title: Analog supply decoupling
circuits.description: VDDA takes its supply with a 0.1 µF capacitor straight across to VSSA, which goes to ground.

operation.text: The CH32V203 is the small- and medium-capacity general-purpose member of WCH's CH32V line, built on the QingKe V4B RISC-V core. Models differ in flash, SRAM, pin count and peripheral count but share software and pin functions.

QingKe V4B runs the RV32IMAC instruction set with machine and user privilege modes, a programmable fast interrupt controller with a hardware interrupt stack, branch prediction, single-cycle multiply, hardware divide, memory protection and custom extended instructions. It scores 465 in CoreMark and draws about 52 µA per MHz.

SRAM holds data and loses it at power-off. Code flash holds the application and constants; part of it runs with zero wait states and the rest with wait states. A 28 KB system flash holds the factory boot loader, and two 128-byte areas hold the non-volatile system configuration and user option bytes.
BOOT0 and BOOT1 pick one of three start-up sources at reset: program flash, system memory or internal SRAM. The boot loader in system memory can rewrite program flash over USART1 or USB.

Where neither BOOT0 nor PB2/BOOT1 reaches a pin, BOOT0 is tied to ground inside and PB2 floats; set PB2 as a pulled-down input to save current in low-power modes. Where only PB2/BOOT1 is bonded out, BOOT0 is grounded inside. Where only BOOT0 is bonded out, PB2/BOOT1 is grounded inside, and PB2 should again be a pulled-down input in low-power modes. Where BOOT0 shares a pin with PB8 or PB9, an external 4.7 kΩ pull-down keeps BOOT0 low at power-up so the chip boots from program flash; afterwards the GPIO may drive an output.

VDD (2.4 V to 3.6 V) powers the regulator and some I/O. VI/O (2.4 V to 3.6 V) powers most I/O and sets their output-high level; it never exceeds VDD while running. VDDA (2.4 V to 3.6 V) powers the HSI, ADC, temperature sensor and PLL, equals VI/O, stays live with VI/O if VDD goes down, and is at least 2.4 V when the ADC runs. VBAT (1.8 V to 3.6 V) is optional and, once VDD is gone, runs the RTC, LSE and backup registers through an internal switch.

A power-on/power-down reset circuit is always active and holds the chip in reset below its threshold, so no external reset part is needed. A programmable voltage detector, enabled in software, compares VDD with a chosen threshold and can raise an interrupt on falling or rising through it.
The internal regulator starts on after reset. It runs normally in Run mode, can be put in a low-power state in Stop mode, and is switched off with a high-impedance output in Standby.
Only the CPU clock stops; peripherals keep running. Any interrupt or wake-up event resumes, and this mode wakes fastest.

Flash goes to low power and the PLL, HSI and HSE stop while SRAM and register contents are kept. Wake sources: any EXTI line (one of the 16 I/O lines, PVD output, RTC alarm, USB or Ethernet wake-up), an NRST reset or an IWDG reset.

The main LDO is off and a low-power LDO feeds only the wake-up logic; other digital circuits and flash lose power. Up to 32 KB of SRAM and the backup registers can be retained, set up before entry. Waking causes a reset and sets SBF in PWR_CSR (cleared by CSBF in PWR_CR). Wake sources: any EXTI line, NRST, an IWDG reset or a rising edge on WKUP.

The 8 MHz HSI is on after reset and is the default system clock; an external 3 MHz to 25 MHz HSE or the PLL can then be chosen. With clock security on, a failed HSE makes the system fall back to HSI and turns off HSE and PLL, with an optional interrupt. After waking from Stop or Standby the chip runs on HSI. HB, PB1 and PB2 clocks reach 144 MHz. The 40 kHz LSI and 32.768 kHz LSE clock the RTC and independent watchdog.
USB needs a 48 MHz clock divided from the PLL, so with USB in use the system clock must be 48, 96 or 144 MHz.

The CH32V203RB takes a 32 MHz crystal or clock on HSE and has its load capacitors inside. Its LSI runs at 32 kHz nominal. Its HSE ÷4 and ÷8 PLL input paths and the ÷5 USB prescaler setting exist only on lots whose fifth digit from the end of the lot number is above zero.
Computes a CRC over 32-bit words with a fixed polynomial, for checking flash contents or data integrity against a signature made at link time.

The PFIC handles up to 255 vectors, currently 8 core and 88 peripheral sources, with a non-maskable interrupt, hardware context stacking, four vector-table-free fast channels, tail chaining and nesting up to 2 levels.
19 edge detectors, each set for rising, falling or both edges and maskable on its own. Up to 37 GPIO pins share 16 external interrupt lines.
An 8-channel general DMA controller with ring-buffer mode serves the timers, ADC, USART, I2C and SPI; DMA and CPU reach SRAM through an arbiter.

The RTC is a 32-bit counter with a 20-bit prescaler, clocked from LSE, LSI or a divided HSE. It and the backup registers sit in the backup domain, fed from VDD or, when VDD fails, from VBAT. With LSE as its clock the RTC keeps time through resets and Standby. Up to 42 16-bit backup registers (84 bytes) survive Standby and resets; a tamper event clears them all.

Two 12-bit ADCs share up to 16 external and 2 internal channels (temperature sensor on IN16 and the internal reference). They convert single, continuous, scan or discontinuous, support dual-ADC mode, an analog watchdog, timer or pin triggers and DMA. Touch-key detection uses the same external channels, up to 16, with software deciding the key state.

The input sees the source resistance RAIN, about 5 pF of pad and board capacitance Cp, the switch resistance RADC and the 8 pF sampling capacitor. A larger Cp costs accuracy; lowering fADC recovers it.

TIM1 is a 16-bit up/down advanced timer with 6 channels of complementary PWM, dead-time insertion, a repetition counter and break input. TIM2 to TIM4 (and the 32-bit TIM5 on the RB) are general-purpose timers with 4 channels each for capture, compare, PWM and one-pulse output, encoder and Hall-sensor inputs. Timers can be chained for synchronisation, and their counters freeze in debug.

The independent watchdog is a 12-bit down counter on the 40 kHz LSI, so it keeps running in Stop and Standby; option bytes can start it in hardware. The 7-bit window watchdog counts down on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt. The core's 64-bit SysTick counts up or down from SYSCLK or SYSCLK/8.

Four USARTs support full-duplex asynchronous, synchronous one-way and single-wire half-duplex links, LIN, ISO7816 smart card, IrDA SIR, CTS/RTS flow control and multiprocessor addressing, with a fractional baud generator and DMA.
Up to two SPIs act as master or slave, multi-master, full or half duplex, 8- or 16-bit frames, with selectable clock polarity and phase, hardware CRC, SD/MMC basic mode and DMA.
Up to two I2C interfaces, master or slave, standard and fast speed, 7- or 10-bit addressing with dual slave address, hardware CRC, DMA and SMBus 2.0/PMBus.

CAN 2.0A and 2.0B active up to 1 Mbit/s with time-triggered mode, 3 transmit mailboxes and two 3-deep receive FIFOs. It has 14 filters and shares a 512-byte SRAM with USBD; with both in use USBD is limited to the lower 384 bytes.

USBD is a full-speed device controller with 16 endpoints, full and low speed, all four transfer types, double buffering and suspend/resume. USBFS is a full-speed controller that works as host or device, with 16 device endpoints plus host endpoints. Both take a 48 MHz clock divided from the PLL, which must run at 48, 96 or 144 MHz.

Each pin can be a push-pull or open-drain output, an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or a peripheral function. All except the analog-capable pins can carry high current. A lock mechanism freezes a port's configuration. Most pins are powered by VI/O, so changing VI/O changes their output-high level.
A GPIO sinks or sources up to ±8 mA within its VOL/VOH limits, and up to ±20 mA with relaxed levels. The sum over all pins must stay within the absolute maximum supply and ground currents.

Two op-amps that can also act as comparators. Their inputs and outputs are selectable among several pins and link internally to the ADC and timers: they can amplify a small signal into the ADC, or compare and send the result to a GPIO or a timer input.
A 2-wire serial debug interface (SDI) on SWDIO and SWCLK is active after power-up or reset; software can release the pins once running.

PC13, PC14 and PC15 are fed through an analog switch from VDD or VBAT that passes at most 3 mA. On VDD, PC14 and PC15 work as GPIO or LSE pins and PC13 as GPIO, tamper input, RTC calibration clock, alarm or second output. On VBAT, PC14 and PC15 serve only the LSE and PC13 only tamper, alarm or second output. As outputs these pins run at 2 MHz into 30 pF at most and cannot source current, so they cannot drive an LED. They start in their main function the first time the backup domain powers up, and after that the backup registers, not the system reset, set their state.

On the CH32V203C6T6, C8T6 and C8U6 (pins 5 and 6) and on the F6P6, G6U6 and K8T6 (pins 2 and 3), OSC_IN and OSC_OUT come up as oscillator pins and software can turn them into PD0 and PD1. The RBT6's oscillator pins cannot become PD0 and PD1.
In the 20- and 28-pin packages some package pins join two I/O functions. Never configure both as outputs at once, or the pin can be damaged; watch the state of both where current matters.
A remapped function ending in _1, _2 or _3 is selected by writing that value to its field in AFIO; TIM2_CH1 and TIM2_ETR share a pin and cannot be used together.

Voltages refer to VSS. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the worst case of temperature, supply and clock; typical figures are for 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V and are a design guide. Figures not marked as tested come from characterisation or design, with minimum and maximum backed by sample tests.
VDD may rise at any rate; it must fall no faster than 20 µs per volt.

Use a crystal of 80 Ω ESR or less, lower preferred. Size the load capacitors to the crystal's specified load; they are normally equal. The HSE starts in about 2.5 ms with an 8 MHz crystal once VDD is stable.
Size the load capacitors to the crystal's specified load; they are usually equal, near 12 pF each. The LSE takes about 800 ms to start once VDD is stable.

Flash programs a 256-byte page in 2 ms and erases a page or a 4 KB sector in 16 ms, at a flash clock (HCLK) of 60 MHz or less. Endurance is at least 10 000 cycles at 25 °C (80 000 measured typical) and retention at least 20 years.
Dimensions are in millimetres. Pin pitch is a nominal figure with no tolerance; other dimensions are within ±0.2 mm or ±10 %, whichever is larger.

CH32 V 2 03 C 8 T 6 reads: CH32 family; V for a QingKe RISC-V general-purpose MCU; 2 for a V4 core without floating point at 144 MHz; 03 general-purpose subfamily; pin-count letter (F 20, G 28, K 32, C 48, R 64); flash letter (6 32 KB, 8 64 KB, B 128 KB); package letter (T for LQFP, U for QFN, R for QSOP, P for TSSOP); temperature digit (6 for -40 to 85 °C, 7 for -40 to 105 °C).
